ESV.2: “Truly I know that it is so: But how can a man be in the right before God?
ESV.3: If one wished to contend with him, one could not answer him once in a thousand times.
ESV.4: He is wise in heart and mighty in strength — who has hardened himself against him, and succeeded? —
ESV.5: he who removes mountains, and they know it not, when he overturns them in his anger,
ESV.6: who shakes the earth out of its place, and its pillars tremble;
ESV.7: who commands the sun, and it does not rise; who seals up the stars;
ESV.8: who alone stretched out the heavens and trampled the waves of the sea;
ESV.9: who made the Bear and Orion, the Pleiades and the chambers of the south;
ESV.10: who does great things beyond searching out, and marvelous things beyond number.
ESV.11: Behold, he passes by me, and I see him not; he moves on, but I do not perceive him.
ESV.12: Behold, he snatches away; who can turn him back? Who will say to him, ‘What are you doing?’
ESV.13: “God will not turn back his anger; beneath him bowed the helpers of Rahab.
ESV.14: How then can I answer him, choosing my words with him?
ESV.15: Though I am in the right, I cannot answer him; I must appeal for mercy to my accuser.
ESV.16: If I summoned him and he answered me, I would not believe that he was listening to my voice.
ESV.17: For he crushes me with a tempest and multiplies my wounds without cause;
ESV.18: he will not let me get my breath, but fills me with bitterness.
ESV.19: If it is a contest of strength, behold, he is mighty! If it is a matter of justice, who can summon him?
ESV.20: Though I am in the right, my own mouth would condemn me; though I am blameless, he would prove me perverse.
ESV.21: I am blameless; I regard not myself; I loathe my life.
ESV.22: It is all one; therefore I say, ‘He destroys both the blameless and the wicked.’
ESV.23: When disaster brings sudden death, he mocks at the calamity  of the innocent.
ESV.24: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked; he covers the faces of its judges — if it is not he, who then is it?
ESV.25: “My days are swifter than a runner; they flee away; they see no good.
ESV.26: They go by like skiffs of reed, like an eagle swooping on the prey.
ESV.27: If I say, ‘I will forget my complaint, I will put off my sad face, and be of good cheer,’
ESV.28: I become afraid of all my suffering, for I know you will not hold me innocent.
ESV.29: I shall be condemned; why then do I labor in vain?
ESV.30: If I wash myself with snow and cleanse my hands with lye,
ESV.31: yet you will plunge me into a pit, and my own clothes will abhor me.
ESV.32: For he is not a man, as I am, that I might answer him, that we should come to trial together.
ESV.33: There is no  arbiter between us, who might lay his hand on us both.
ESV.34: Let him take his rod away from me, and let not dread of him terrify me.
ESV.35: Then I would speak without fear of him, for I am not so in myself.

AMP.2:
"Yes, I know it is true.
But how can a mortal man be right before God?
AMP.3:
"If one should want to contend or dispute with Him,
He could not answer Him once in a thousand times.
AMP.4:
"God is wise in heart and mighty in strength;
Who has [ever] defied or challenged Him and remained unharmed?
AMP.5:
"It is God who removes the mountains, and they do not know it,
When He overturns them in His anger;
AMP.6:
Who shakes the earth out of its place,
And its pillars tremble;
AMP.7:
Who commands the sun, and it does not shine;
Who seals up the stars [from view];
AMP.8:
Who alone stretches out the heavens
And tramples down the waves of the sea;
AMP.9:
Who made [the constellations] the Bear, Orion, and the Pleiades,
And the [vast starry] spaces of the south;
AMP.10:
Who does great things, [beyond understanding,] unfathomable,
Yes, marvelous and wondrous things without number.
AMP.11:
"Behold, He passes by me, and I do not see Him;
He moves past me, but I do not perceive Him.
AMP.12:
"Behold, He snatches away; who can restrain or turn Him back?
Who will say to Him, 'What are You doing?'
AMP.13:
"God will not turn back His anger;
The [proud] helpers of Rahab [the arrogant monster of the sea] bow under Him.
AMP.14:
"How can I answer Him [and plead my case],
Choosing my words [to reason] with Him?
AMP.15:
For though I were righteous, I could not answer.
I must appeal for mercy to my Opponent and Judge.
AMP.16:
"If I called and He answered me,
I could not believe that He was listening to my voice.
AMP.17:
"For He bruises me with a tempest
And multiplies my wounds without cause.
AMP.18:
"He will not allow me to catch my breath,
But fills and saturates me with bitterness.
AMP.19:
"If it is a matter of strength and power, behold, He is mighty!
And if of justice, who can summon and challenge Him?
AMP.20:
"Though I am innocent and in the right, my own mouth would pronounce me guilty;
Though I am blameless, He would denounce me as guilty.
AMP.21:
"[Though] I am blameless,
I do not care about myself;
I despise my life.
AMP.22:
"It is all one; therefore I say,
'He destroys [both] the blameless and the wicked.'
AMP.23:
"When [His] scourge kills suddenly,
He mocks at the despair of the innocent.
AMP.24:
"The earth is given into the hands of the wicked;
He covers the faces of its judges [so that they are blind to justice].
If it is not He, then who is it [that is responsible for all this injustice]?
AMP.25:
"Now my days are swifter than a runner;
They vanish, they see no good.

NLT.2:

NLT.4:

NLT.5:
“Without warning, he moves the mountains,
overturning them in his anger.
NLT.6:
He shakes the earth from its place,
and its foundations tremble.
NLT.7:
If he commands it, the sun won’t rise
and the stars won’t shine.
NLT.8:
He alone has spread out the heavens
and marches on the waves of the sea.
NLT.9:
He made all the stars — the Bear and Orion,
the Pleiades and the constellations of the southern sky.
NLT.10:
He does great things too marvelous to understand.
He performs countless miracles.
NLT.11:
“Yet when he comes near, I cannot see him.
When he moves by, I do not see him go.
NLT.12:
If he snatches someone in death, who can stop him?
Who dares to ask, ‘What are you doing?’
NLT.13:

Even the monsters of the sea are crushed beneath his feet.
NLT.14:
“So who am I, that I should try to answer God
or even reason with him?
NLT.15:
Even if I were right, I would have no defense.
I could only plead for mercy.
NLT.16:

I’m not sure he would listen to me.
NLT.17:

and repeatedly wounds me without cause.
NLT.18:
He will not let me catch my breath,
but fills me instead with bitter sorrows.
NLT.19:
If it’s a question of strength, he’s the strong one.
If it’s a matter of justice, who dares to summon him to court?
NLT.20:
Though I am innocent, my own mouth would pronounce me guilty.
Though I am blameless, it would prove me wicked.
NLT.21:
“I am innocent,
but it makes no difference to me —

NLT.22:
Innocent or wicked, it is all the same to God.

NLT.23:
When a plague sweeps through,

NLT.24:
The whole earth is in the hands of the wicked,
and God blinds the eyes of the judges.

NLT.25:
“My life passes more swiftly than a runner.

NLT.26:

like an eagle swooping down on its prey.
NLT.27:
If I decided to forget my complaints,
to put away my sad face and be cheerful,
NLT.28:
I would still dread all the pain,
for I know you will not find me innocent, O God.
NLT.29:
Whatever happens, I will be found guilty.
So what’s the use of trying?
NLT.30:
Even if I were to wash myself with soap
and clean my hands with lye,
NLT.31:
you would plunge me into a muddy ditch,
and my own filthy clothing would hate me.
NLT.32:
“God is not a mortal like me,
so I cannot argue with him or take him to trial.
NLT.33:
If only there were a mediator between us,
someone who could bring us together.
NLT.34:
The mediator could make God stop beating me,
and I would no longer live in terror of his punishment.
NLT.35:
Then I could speak to him without fear,
but I cannot do that in my own strength.

MSG.2:
"So what's new? I know all this.
The question is, 'How can mere mortals get right with God?'
MSG.3:
If we wanted to bring our case before him,
what chance would we have? Not one in a thousand!
MSG.4:
God's wisdom is so deep, God's power so immense,
who could take him on and come out in one piece?
MSG.5:
He moves mountains before they know what's happened,
flips them on their heads on a whim.
MSG.6:
He gives the earth a good shaking up,
rocks it down to its very foundations.
MSG.7:
He tells the sun, 'Don't shine,' and it doesn't;
he pulls the blinds on the stars.
MSG.8:
All by himself he stretches out the heavens
and strides on the waves of the sea.
MSG.9:
He designed the Big Dipper and Orion,
the Pleiades and Alpha Centauri.
MSG.10:
We'll never comprehend all the great things he does;
his miracle-surprises can't be counted.
MSG.11:
Somehow, though he moves right in front of me, I don't see him;
quietly but surely he's active, and I miss it.
MSG.12:
If he steals you blind, who can stop him?
Who's going to say, 'Hey, what are you doing?'
MSG.13:
God doesn't hold back on his anger;
even dragon-bred monsters cringe before him.
MSG.14:
"So how could I ever argue with him,
construct a defense that would influence God?
MSG.15:
Even though I'm innocent I could never prove it;
I can only throw myself on the Judge's mercy.
MSG.16:
If I called on God and he himself answered me,
then, and only then, would I believe that he'd heard me.
MSG.17:
As it is, he knocks me about from pillar to post,
beating me up, black and blue, for no good reason.
MSG.18:
He won't even let me catch my breath,
piles bitterness upon bitterness.
MSG.19:
If it's a question of who's stronger, he wins, hands down!
If it's a question of justice, who'll serve him the subpoena?
MSG.20:
Even though innocent, anything I say incriminates me;
blameless as I am, my defense just makes me sound worse.
MSG.21:
"Believe me, I'm blameless.
I don't understand what's going on.
I hate my life!
MSG.22:
Since either way it ends up the same, I can only conclude
that God destroys the good right along with the bad.
MSG.23:
When calamity hits and brings sudden death,
he folds his arms, aloof from the despair of the innocent.
MSG.24:
He lets the wicked take over running the world,
he installs judges who can't tell right from wrong.
If he's not responsible, who is?
MSG.25:
"My time is short—what's left of my life races off
too fast for me to even glimpse the good.
MSG.26:
My life is going fast, like a ship under full sail,
like an eagle plummeting to its prey.
MSG.27:
Even if I say, 'I'll put all this behind me,
I'll look on the bright side and force a smile,'
MSG.28:
All these troubles would still be like grit in my gut
since it's clear you're not going to let up.
MSG.29:
The verdict has already been handed down—'Guilty!'—
so what's the use of protests or appeals?
MSG.30:
Even if I scrub myself all over
and wash myself with the strongest soap I can find,
MSG.31:
It wouldn't last—you'd push me into a pigpen, or worse,
so nobody could stand me for the stink.
MSG.32:
"God and I are not equals; I can't bring a case against him.
We'll never enter a courtroom as peers.
MSG.33:
How I wish we had an arbitrator
to step in and let me get on with life—
MSG.34:
To break God's death grip on me,
to free me from this terror so I could breathe again.
MSG.35:
Then I'd speak up and state my case boldly.
As things stand, there is no way I can do it.
